study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify regional subcortical brain volume anomalies in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) using normative modeling, assess the relative sensitivity and specificity of abnormal volumes in discriminating FASD from comparison group, and examine associations with cognitive function.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (87 datasets; ENIGMA Lifespan WG and collaborators)
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Individual regional volumetric z-scores were generated using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024), an open source online software tool that leverages an aggregated neuroimaging dataset with a large number of individuals (37,407 comparison brains). Z-scores (M = 0, SD = 1) were calculated for each of the 7 bilateral subcortical regions... The training data used in creating the CentileBrain model were primarily collected from the Enhancing Neuroimaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis (ENIGMA) Consortium (Ge et al., 2024)... The CentileBrain model is based on structural imaging data from 87 datasets.

rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Unexpectedly, our participants (including those in the comparison group) demonstrated smaller than expected norm-corrected subcortical volumes (mean z-scores for those in the comparison group were negative as opposed to zero) in several regions including the left and right putamen and the right pallidum. These lower than expected z-scores could be due to differences in image acquisition and processing... Our preprocessing workflow included some steps (i.e., intensity normalization and gradient distortion correction using the proprietary Siemens gradient table), which may not have been performed in some of the datasets that informed the CentileBrain model. Additionally, while the HCP Minimal Preprocessing Pipelines are based around FreeSurfer version 6.0, many of the datasets used for CentileBrain were processed using either older or more recent versions of FreeSurfer (≤5.3 or ≥7.1) (Ge et al., 2024). Small differences across FreeSurfer versions, as well as the optional arguments used during processing, may have a significant impact on morphometric analyses and may explain the smaller than expected volumes we observed across both groups of participants in some subcortical structures (Filip et al., 2022)... Despite the systematic difference between our data and the normative data, we were still able to detect that the FASD group had smaller subcortical volumes than the comparison group.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Youth with FASD showed more and larger-magnitude reductions in regional subcortical volumes than comparisons, especially in bilateral hippocampi and caudate; small-volume thresholds identified a substantial subset of FASD cases and volumes related to cognition within groups.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study's limitations include a non-generalizable, convenience sample (FASD vs. controls); unmeasured confounding from polysubstance exposure and socioeconomic status (SES); racial disparities between groups; a narrow focus on subcortical regions; and systematic negative shifts in z-scores, likely due to methodological differences between the study's data acquisition/processing and that of the heterogeneous datasets used to create the CentileBrain normative model.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are several limitations of this study... Participants in this study were recruited based on a history of PAE or being typically-developing... Polysubstance exposure is common... We did not have access to detailed information about tobacco exposures... there was a higher proportion of White participants in the comparison group vs. the FASD group, potentially introducing bias... we focused our examination on subcortical regions of interest... It is also important to note that we found systematically smaller norm-corrected subcortical volumes in our participants, likely reflecting differences in image acquisition and processing differences with the heterogeneous samples used by CentileBrain, which represents a limitation of this study.
